semantics.framing: a record is one JSON document plus a newline; input may arrive in any chunking; a record past the caller's buffer or the 16 MiB raw frame limit is dropped as too_large and framing resyncs at the next newline; a blank line is not a record; a trailing CR is trimmed
semantics.writing: one lock per record covers the record and its newline, so records from concurrent jobs never interleave; a slow reader blocks the writer instead of mixing or dropping bytes; a record containing a newline is refused
semantics.decoding: UTF-8 and nesting depth are checked over the raw bytes before the parser runs; duplicate members, a missing or wrong jsonrpc, a bad id type, over-long methods and ids and trailing bytes are JSON-RPC errors; params are captured raw and decoded once the method is known
semantics.arguments: decoded against contracts/tools.json; unknown fields, wrong types, numbers outside the schema range, missing required fields and more than 32 batch items are tool errors with E_INVALID_ARGUMENT, because the request itself was well formed
semantics.handshake: only 2025-11-25 is accepted and any other version is refused by name; a second initialize is -32600; tools/list and tools/call before initialize are -32600
semantics.discovery: only enabled tools are advertised, taken from the embedded contract with outputSchema removed; patch and create stay disabled until T12; an unknown or disabled tool is a tool error with E_UNSUPPORTED
semantics.execution: every call authorizes through I01, reserves through I02 before allocating, registers itself in the Registry, and runs I03-I06 with that cancellation; the result is the T07 logical response in one text block, with isError set for failures
semantics.cancellation: notifications/cancelled reaches only an in-flight request of the same session; anything else is counted as cancel_ignored and ignored
semantics.memory: one arena per request bounded by Caps.request_bytes, plus a fixed logical-response buffer and a fixed record buffer; a call's output budget is capped at Caps.output_bytes

exports: zcr_mcp (src/protocol/mcp.zig): protocol_version, server_name, server_version, output_profile, tools_json, Tools, Caps, Report, Registry, Dependencies, Server{init, deinit, serveFrame (core.ServeFrameFn), report}
zcr_mcp.framing: max_frame_bytes, Framer{init, next, pending, records, oversize}, Writer{init, writeRecord, records, bytes}
zcr_mcp.codec: Id, Method, Tool, Args, Request, Fault, Decoded, decode, encodeResult, encodeToolResult, encodeError, encodeEnvelope, toolResultBytes, max_depth, rpc_* codes
limitations: serveFrame serves one record at a time on the calling task; a reader loop, per-session queues and concurrent tool execution belong to T09
the zcr mcp CLI is not wired up: src/main.zig is integrator-owned and still exits EX_UNAVAILABLE, so no end-to-end host transcript was produced (G07 stays open)
server_version is a constant in this module; the integrator owns the real build version through build_options
status returns a fixed read_only snapshot and no receipt lookup (T11/T12), and health reports pressure normal with the budget's own counters
deadline_ms is decoded and carried but not enforced; a deadline must be expressed through cancellation (same gap as T04 and T07)
structured_compat, resources, prompts, progress notifications and tools/list pagination are not implemented
one text block per result is built in a fixed buffer, so a call's output is capped by Caps.output_bytes (256 KiB by default) even when the request asks for more
the 16 MiB frame limit test allocates one oversize frame in the test process; no host actually sent it
Linux and Intel macOS are cross-compiled only
